meta.title: NRR is same-customer revenue later
meta.summary: SAMPLE start $100k, later $130k from those accounts → 130% NRR. Expansion can exceed 100%.

success.message:
Session complete. NRR = later revenue from the same customers ÷ starting revenue. Can be over 100%.

SAMPLE: 130%; new logos stay out.

start.message:
SAMPLE: a cohort starts at $100k. A year later those same accounts are $130k.

NRR?

choices.label: 130% — ending ÷ starting from the same customers
Logo retention: they kept 100% of customers so NRR is 100%

wrong_start_30.message:
NRR is a retention index around 100, not the delta. 130/100=130%.

Return to the ratio.

wrong_start_logo.message:
NRR is revenue, including expansion. Logos can stay flat while dollars grow.

Return to the ratio.

new.message:
The company also added $50k from brand-new customers.

Does that enter NRR?

choices.label: No — NRR is the starting cohort only
Count half the new revenue as expansion

wrong_new_yes.message:
That would be a company-level growth rate. NRR holds the cohort still.

Revisit new logos.

wrong_new_half.message:
New logos are not expansion of the starting cohort.

Revisit new logos.

check.message:
Start $100k, later $80k from those accounts (churn/contraction).

NRR?

wrong_check_20.message:
20% is the drop. NRR is what remains: 80%.

Try the check again.

wrong_check_180.message:
Do not add the two snapshots.

Try the check again.
